newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: PRESS DIGEST - South Africa - July 23.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - South Africa - July 23.

text.p: These are the leading stories in the South African press on Wednesday.
Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.

- With 12 miners confirmed dead, another six were still missing, presumed dead, last night after a massive underground rockfall at the Hartebeestfontein gold mine near Stilfontein in North West on Monday morning.

- Telkom awarded a two billion rand contract for radio systems to Alcatel Altech Telecoms and Lucent Technologies on Tuesday, moving its project to deliver 2,8 million new phone lines by March 2002 into top gear.

- The Dow Jones industrial average roared back above 8,000 points on Tuesday after U.S. Federal Reserve chairman Alan Greenspan took a non-threatening tone in his mid-year Humphrey-Hawkins economic report to Congress.

- President Nelson Mandela met jailed East Timorese rebel leader Jose Xanana Gusmao during his visit to Indonesia last week, throwing his weight behind international efforts to secure a peaceful resolution to the conflict.

- Deputy President Thabo Mbeki, 10 cabinet ministers, two deputy ministers and at least 100 other officials are set to descend on Washington next week to meet U.S. counterparts they last saw just five months ago in Cape Town.
- Western Areas, the flagship gold mine of JCI Ltd, has restructured its gold hedge to take advantage of any rise in the gold price.
- New Clicks Holdings Ltd has bought Compact Disc Wherehouse, the specialist store.
- Billiton Plc, the demerged base metals and coal operations of Gencor, has become one of the largest mining houses in the world after its successful listing in London.

- Billiton shares on Tuesday made a glistening debut on the London Stock Exchange despite media reports and statements by brokers in London that the share, at its issue price of 220 pennies per share, was over valued.

- Telkom's activity on the capital and money markets incurred an unexpected hitch just after the telecommunications giant sold 30 percent of its shares to an overseas consortium for billions of rands.
- Dan Mobote, the man who confessed to killing seven-year -old Mamokgethi Malebane, was freed on 2,000 rand bail in March even though police opposed bail for the rape suspect.
- The battle to succeed Gauteng Premier Tokyo Sexwale has intensified with one of the candidates, who failed to get the ANC alliance's nod for the job, vowing to put up a fight.
